page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc9i.4xlarge belongs to the High Clock Speed instance family, built on the KVM hypervisor platform. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs backed by Intel Xeon 6982P-C processors on the x86_64 architecture, maintaining a clock frequency of 3.4 GHz. The instance delivers focused computational capability designed specifically for processing-intensive demands.

Memory configuration is set at 32.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 2.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is not included, which means all persistent file systems must rely on external cloud storage infrastructure. Network interfaces deliver a baseline throughput of 16 Gbps, supporting high-bandwidth communication with external services, storage targets, and distributed cluster nodes. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs provisioned on this instance type.

By pairing elevated clock frequencies with a lean memory profile and omitting local disks, the ecs.hfc9i.4xlarge avoids resource overprovisioning for tasks that do not demand extensive RAM pools or fast local NVMe cache. This makes it an efficient option for compute-bound engineering workloads. Representative applications include continuous integration build runners, software compilation pipelines, CPU-intensive microservices, batch processing, and latency-sensitive web server deployments.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc9i.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server from the High Clock Speed family, powered by the KVM hypervisor. The instance is equipped with 16 dedicated vCPUs running on x86_64 Intel Xeon 6982P-C processors clocked at 3.4 GHz, accompanied by 32.0 GB of system memory. Operating with a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per core, the architecture prioritizes processing density over memory capacity. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 16 Gbps, while graphics hardware and integrated local storage are omitted entirely, necessitating network-attached storage volumes for file persistence. This architectural balance provides efficient resource utilization for CPU-bound computational pipelines without the overhead of unused memory or local disks. It is suited for compute-heavy workloads such as continuous integration and build systems, code compilation, video encoding, gaming server hosting, and high-concurrency web application serving.
